source_lines_after.34: [[lem-sl2-structure-and-root-coordinates|Structure of $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and root coordinates]]). The fundamental weight is
source_lines_after.51: **Given:** AC; a field $k$, $G=\mathrm{SL}_2$ with diagonal torus $T_2$, upper triangular Borel $B=T_2\ltimes U^+$, root groups $U^+=\{\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\}$ and $U^-=\{\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\a&1\end{pmatrix}\}$, and a prime $p=\operatorname{char}(k)>0$ in the last part.
source_lines_after.53: [F1] *Root coordinates of $\mathrm{SL}_2$.* $X(T_2)=\mathbb Z\chi$, $\Phi=\{\pm2\chi\}$, $\alpha=2\chi$, $\alpha^\vee=\chi^\vee$ with $\langle\chi,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$, the Weyl group is $\{1,s_\alpha\}$ acting by $s_\alpha(\chi)=\chi-\langle\chi,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha=-\chi$, $u_\alpha(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $u_{-\alpha}(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\a&1\end{pmatrix}$, and $\mathrm{SL}_2$ is generated by $U^+$ and $U^-$ ([[lem-sl2-structure-and-root-coordinates|Structure of $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and root coordinates]], [[def-root-datum-of-a-split-reductive-group]]).
source_lines_after.75: 1.1 With the identification $X(T_2)=\mathbb Z\chi$ of [F1], the fundamental weight is $\omega=\chi$ and $X(T_2)^+=\{m\chi:m\ge0\}$, so [F2] gives the simple modules $L(m)=V(m\chi)$ for $m\ge0$. The trivial representation is one-dimensional hence simple with highest weight $0$, so $L(0)$ is the trivial representation. The standard representation $k^2$ is simple: for any nonzero $v=(a,b)$ one has $\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\b&a^{-1}\end{pmatrix}e_1=v$ when $a\ne0$ and $\begin{pmatrix}0&-b^{-1}\\b&0\end{pmatrix}e_1=v$ when $a=0$, so the submodule generated by any nonzero vector is all of $k^2$; moreover $e_1$ is fixed by $U^+$ and is a $T_2$-eigenvector of weight $\chi$, so $e_1$ is primitive of weight $\chi=\omega$ and $k^2\cong L(1)$ by [F2]. [F1, F2]
